Marathon Petroleum fell 3% today after climbing sharply over the prior three trading days (up roughly 3% from November 11 to November 13). The decline follows geopolitical escalation in the Middle East—Iran has ramped up threats as a third U.S. carrier arrived in the Persian Gulf—which typically pressures oil refiners by raising uncertainty around crude supplies and global demand. U.S. oil prices dropped to $89.62 per barrel today, down from recent highs, removing tailwinds that had supported the stock's recent run.

Refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, near peak levels, which limits upside from production increases if energy demand slows. The sharp rise in heating oil prices this winter (up 59% year-over-year) had been a bright spot for refiners, but broader economic caution—reflected in retailers pulling back holiday inventory due to rising shipping costs—suggests demand headwinds may be building, which would weigh on a refiner's margins and throughput.
